reasons: internal/analyzer/resourcesummary.go:42-47 PodResourceNumbers now applies the init-container max rule to LIMITS as well as requests. The max rule is correct for scheduling/capacity/cost (what the PR set out to fix), but LimCPUm/LimMemB feed runtime consumers that compare *running-container* metrics against them, so the pod is now measured against a limit no running container enforces. Concrete: pod with initContainer 'load-model' limits memory 8Gi and container 'app' limits memory 1Gi. main returns LimMemB=1Gi (the value the app container actually OOMKills at); HEAD returns 8Gi. The PR's own new test (internal/analyzer/capacity_effective_request_test.go:75) asserts exactly this new behavior (init 2Gi wins over app 512Mi), so it is confirmed, not hypothetical.

internal/analyzer/predictive_incident.go:52,60 consequence of the above: PodCPUSaturation / PodMemorySaturation and the 24h PredictedCPU/MemoryExhaustion drafts divide pod-level metric usage by q.LimCPUm / q.LimMemB. With app limit 1Gi and an init limit of 8Gi, a pod sitting at 950Mi used to trip the 0.9 ratio and emit a critical 'PodMemorySaturation' draft; it now computes 950Mi/8Gi = 0.12 and emits nothing. The alert is silently lost, with no test covering it and no mention in scripts/changelog.txt.

internal/proxy/admin_k8s_resource_advisor.go:81 -> internal/analyzer/resourceadvisor.go:86,129 same root cause on the advisor path: the CPU-throttling rule (UsageCPUm >= LimCPUm*throttleNearLimit) stops firing when an init container declares a larger CPU limit than the app containers, and the OOMKilled recommendation renders rec.Current = FormatMemBytes(in.LimMemB) — i.e. it tells the operator the pod's 'current memory limit' is the init container's 8Gi while the container that just OOMKilled is capped at 1Gi.

internal/analyzer/resourcesummary.go:28-33 the doc comment justifying the change is backwards for the case it names: 'the operator triaging an OOMKill saw a memory limit smaller than the one the pod actually holds'. For OOMKill triage the relevant number is the app container's limit, which is exactly what main returned; HEAD replaces it with a value the running container does not hold. scripts/changelog.txt repeats the same claim. Behaviour and stated rationale disagree.
notes: The request-side half of the PR is correct and well covered. I re-ran internal/analyzer/capacity_effective_request_test.go against a scratch worktree of main: 5 of the 6 tests fail there with the exact deltas the changelog claims (2600m vs 2000m, node packing 125% / GPU Idle:-3, cost 2 pods / 68000 vs 34000, qtyMem("1T")=0), and TestNativeSidecarRequestIsAddedNotMaxed passes as the declared regression guard. The tests genuinely exercise the change; item 1 of the review checklist is satisfied.

podReservesResources (capacity.go:307-320) is sound on the real data path — kube.InventoryFromObject (internal/kube/client.go:484) always sets StatusObject from raw .status, ListK8sInventory selects status_json (internal/store/k8s.go:478), and the agent path reuses the same constructor (internal/agent/runner.go:422) — so .phase is present in practice. But the fallback comment at capacity.go:315 ('the collector summarizes a Pod's status as its phase') is false: kube.summarizeStatus (internal/kube/client.go:548-556) returns podWaitingReason first, so a completed Job pod's Status is "Completed", not "Succeeded". If StatusObject were ever empty the fallback would not catch the main case it exists for. Latent, not currently reachable.
podDeclaresResources including initContainers in HasReq/HasLim is defensible — Kubernetes QoS also considers init containers — so I did not count that as a defect.

effectivePodTotal ignores sidecars that started before a given init container when computing largestInit; K8s uses max over (init_i + sum of preceding sidecars). Slight underestimate in a rare shape; not blocking.

No migrations, no external state, no auth/secret/delete paths touched — a revert is a clean code revert. The version bump (internal/proxy/server.go:35), docs/K8S_OPERATIONS_HUB.md and scripts/changelog.txt match this repo's per-release convention and are not scope creep.
go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./internal/analyzer ./internal/proxy ./internal/store all pass on HEAD — the regressions above are unguarded by any existing test.

Suggested minimal fix: keep effectivePodTotal for requests, and revert LimCPUm/LimMemB in PodResourceNumbers to the regular-containers sum (or expose both an effective total and a running-container total, letting predictive_incident.go and the resource advisor use the latter).
